comment: Could this preserve the type of the parsed URL components? When `self._r.url` is a bytes URL, `urlparse()` returns bytes components, but `to_native_string()` always makes the Host a native `str` on Python 3. Passing the mixed bytes/str components to `urlunparse()` raises `TypeError`; the previous conditional conversion avoided mixing types for bytes URLs.

Could this retain the `getattr(cls, "task_namespace", None)` guard? Directly accessing `cls.task_namespace` raises `AttributeError` when `Register` is used to create a class that does not define or inherit that attribute, whereas the previous code treated that case as an unset namespace and applied the default.

Removing the `deepcopy` makes `result[DATA]` a serialized JSON string on the original `reply.result`. That mutated object is subsequently passed to `storeTxnInGraph(reply.result)` and used in the client reply, whereas the previous code preserved the original structured data for those paths. Could the serialized copy be kept limited to the ledger path instead of mutating `reply.result`?

By removing the `not build_directory` check, a `setup_build()` implementation that returns `True` without setting `BUILD_DIR` will now proceed with `Runner(None, context)` instead of raising `CorpusPruningException`. Please retain the environment-value validation (or explicitly guarantee and enforce that `setup_build()` always populates `BUILD_DIR`).
The formatted message opens a parenthesized section before `CP` but never closes it after `NCP: {}`. This produces malformed `pokemon_appeared` output; add the missing `)` to the format string.

This changes the helper name from the correctly spelled `next_occurrence` to `next_ocurrance`, which can break any existing test calls or references to `next_occurrence`. Please keep the original spelling (or update all callers consistently if the typo exists elsewhere).

Could this use a clearer format such as `Value for header %s (%s) ...` or quote the name and value? `Value for header {foo:bar}` looks like a dictionary literal, and the missing space after the colon makes the header name and value harder to distinguish, especially when either contains punctuation.

The setting documentation still says “This setting requires a restart,” while the implementation applies the change dynamically for non-Wayland platforms and only requires a restart on Wayland. Please update this text to match the conditional behavior described in `configdata.yml`.

After creating a new agent, the result of `explode_agents(...)` is discarded, so `agent` is still empty when the unconditional `agent[0]['sleep']` access runs. This causes an `IndexError` on the first heartbeat from every newly seen agent; assign the exploded result back to `agent` (or use the returned row directly).

Changing `core_agent` from `sleep` to `sleep_min`/`sleep_max` via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` does not migrate existing databases: existing tables retain `sleep` and lack the new columns, causing agent reads or the new jitter calculation to fail. Please add an explicit schema migration (including data conversion, if needed).

`TypeSlots.special_method_names` is populated with `set(get_slot_table(...))`, and `SlotTable.__iter__()` yields slot descriptor objects rather than method-name strings. Therefore this string membership test is always false, so special methods no longer dispatch through their `slot...` handlers when no regular method handler is found. Populate the set from the method-name mapping (or expose a dedicated name collection) instead.

`six.u` was removed from `luigi/six.py` in this PR, so both calls in the `unbatched_params` branch will raise `AttributeError` when that batch mode is used. Please keep the native string formatting used by the surrounding implementation instead of reintroducing `six.u`.

Could this be phrased as “Verify that gradients with respect to the image are nonzero”? The test no longer runs an optimization, and the current “Making sure…” wording is an awkward fragment that does not describe the specific assertion.

The `# doctest: +IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL` line is now an expected-output line, not a doctest directive, because it lacks a `>>>` prompt. This will make the doctest expect the comment as part of the traceback output and will not enable `IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL`; place the directive on the preceding `>>> obj.unwrap(...)` line instead.
Please fix the typos in this comment: `pipline` should be `pipeline`, and `unmmaped` should be `unmapped`.

`graph` is defined as a read-only `@property` that returns `self._graph`, so assigning `self.graph = ...` here raises `AttributeError: can't set attribute` during processing. Assign to `self._graph` (or add a setter and update all related accesses) instead.
Please retain the space after the comment marker (`# insert ...`) to follow standard Python formatting and keep this comment consistent with surrounding code.

`KINESIS_RETURN_ERRORS = True` creates a new local variable in `start_test`; it does not update the flag read by `infra.update_kinesis`, so throttling will never be injected. Set the shared module/infra flag explicitly (and restore it in a `finally` block).

Removing `ERROR_PROBABILITY` from `localstack/constants.py` will break any remaining callers that import or reference this shared constant. Please update those callers to the new mechanism, or retain the constant until all references are removed.

By removing these assertions, `create_from_edges` no longer enforces the supplied `urange`/`vrange` when `validate=False`. In particular, `heterograph()` constructs each relation with `validate=False`, so an edge whose node ID exceeds `num_nodes_dict` can now bypass the boundary check and reach `create_unitgraph_from_coo` instead of raising `DGLError`. Please preserve a boundary check for the `heterograph` construction path, or validate the complete heterograph before creating its relation graphs.

In `_store_iam_policy`, `db_members` contains member model objects, but this condition compares the string `member` against that list: `member not in db_members`. As a result, a policy containing case variants such as `user/A@example.com` and `user/a@example.com` can append the same cached member object twice after both keys are lowercased. Compare the cached object (or track normalized member keys) before appending.

Uncommenting `setup_test_logging()` makes importing this test module globally configure the process root logger. This can add handlers before other tests or modules initialize their own logging and cause order-dependent behavior; prefer invoking the setup from the test fixture (or using isolated logging configuration) rather than at import time.

The new assertion rejects an otherwise valid empty-ROI batch: when `rois` has shape `(0, 5)`, `img_ids.numel()` is `0` while `len(img_metas)` is still the batch size. It also fails when only some images have no ROIs. Since this method is now reachable for images with zero detections, please handle the empty/per-image-empty case explicitly rather than requiring every image ID to appear in `rois`.

`check_symbols_cached` expects `build_params_check_path` to be the `.cached_build_params` file, but this call passes `symbols_directory` itself. As a result, `read_data_from_file` attempts to read the directory rather than the cache file, causing the local-cache check to fail (and potentially raising an error) on every system-symbols lookup. Construct and pass `os.path.join(symbols_directory, '.cached_build_params')` here.

`_update_auth_constraint` still reads `self._update_state_by_versions`, but this attribute is no longer initialized after these lines are removed. Any auth-rule update handled by `AbstractAuthRuleHandler` will now raise `AttributeError` instead of updating state. Please either retain the initialization or refactor `_update_auth_constraint` so it no longer depends on the removed mapping.
`GOAL_STATE_AGENT_VERSION` is no longer referenced after replacing `goal_state_version`, but it remains imported in this module. Please remove the unused import to keep the dependency list accurate.
`is_linux` is no longer referenced after removing the platform check in `startup`; please remove it from the `bzt.utils` import to avoid an unused import.

The documented `ANSIBLE_FILTER_PLUGINS` project path is still `$project_directory/filter/plugins/`, but the implementation now uses `$project_directory/plugins/filter`. Please update the example so it reflects the actual default path.

The documented `ANSIBLE_LIBRARY` ephemeral path is `$ephemeral_directory/modules/`, while `default_env()` still adds the scenario ephemeral `library` directory. Please make the documentation match the generated environment, or update the implementation if `modules` is intended.

`RestService` already defines `update_config` with the same behavior. This second definition shadows the earlier method and creates two sources of truth; please keep a single implementation and place it alongside the other public service methods.

When `cross_valid` is true and `fold` is set, this now unconditionally accesses `self.fold_start_idx`, which is only initialized when `split_ratio` is provided. Previously this path returned `None` (albeit marked WIP), so callers using cross-validation without split metadata will now raise `AttributeError`. Please either initialize the fold boundaries for this mode or preserve/explicitly reject the unsupported path.

This change only swaps the `if`/`elif` branches: for both values of `background`, it performs exactly the same operation as before (`tab_index_changed.emit(...)` when true and `setCurrentWidget(tab)` when false). Therefore it does not change the statusbar update behavior or fix the reported issue. Please adjust the signal emission/order or include the missing behavioral change.

`ab.pop('plugin', plugin)` removes any `plugin` value declared in the ability YAML but discards it, so the subsequently passed `plugin` is always derived from the filename. If the field is intended to be supported in ability data, assign the popped value (or otherwise define which source takes precedence) instead of ignoring it.

Could we retain the `torch.__version__ < '1.3'` condition here? Removing it changes the behavior for supported PyTorch versions below 1.3: batch-normalization modules are still converted to FP32, but their inputs are no longer cast to FP32 before `forward`, which can cause dtype errors or lose the intended FP16 compatibility. The Parrots check can be added without dropping this existing compatibility path.

`kwargs['colors'] = kwargs.pop('bbox_color', 'green')` overwrites an explicitly supplied `colors` argument whenever `bbox_color` is absent. Previously, callers could pass `colors` through to `mmcv.imshow_bboxes`; please preserve that value (while still mapping `bbox_color` when provided).

`handle_user_artist()` still calls `new_user_stats()`, but this patch renames the function to `is_new_user_stats_batch()`. Update the call site as well, otherwise handling a user-artist message raises `NameError`.

The `__repr__` implementation is being removed from `Proxy`, so `Proxy` instances will no longer include `none_ok` and `valid_values` in their representation. The new method is defined on the preceding class instead; is this relocation intentional, or should `Proxy` retain its existing `__repr__`?

Renaming this function from `test_random` to `layer_test_esn` means it no longer matches pytest's default `test_*` discovery pattern, so the parameterized ESN test will not run. Please keep the `test_` prefix (for example, `test_esn`).
